Exercise A

Listening: Sports Day

You will hear each recording twice, just like in the real MSA exam. Listen carefully, then answer the questions below — you won't be able to play a recording more than twice.

💡 Exam tip: In the real exam you hear each recording exactly twice — use the first play to get the general gist, then the second to fill in exact details, rather than trying to catch everything at once.

Part 1 — Comprehension Questions

Exercise B

Reading: Events & Notices

Read the texts below, then answer the questions — just like Reading Parts 1 and 2 in the real MSA exam.

Part 1 — Match the Student to the Event

Sprint (100m): A fast, short race straight down the track — it is over in a matter of seconds. Perfect for students who love pure speed.

Long Jump: Sprint down the runway and leap as far as you can into the sand pit. Timing and technique matter as much as strength.

Shot Put: Throw a heavy metal ball as far as possible. This event is all about power and strength, not running.

Relay Race: A team event in which four runners take turns and pass a baton to each other. You win or lose together.

1 Noah is the strongest boy in his class and loves throwing things. He should try the .

2 Aisha is very quick over short distances and wants a race that finishes fast. She should try the .

3 Leon prefers working with his friends rather than competing on his own. He should try the .

4 Zoe is a good jumper and enjoys landing in the sand. She should try the .

Part 2 — Sports Day Notices: True or False?

🧴 Free sun cream is available at the first-aid tent — please put it on before your events.

🚑 If you feel unwell, go to the first-aid tent, which is next to the changing rooms.

🥤 Water is free all day, but snacks from the stall must be paid for.

🏅 Medals will be given to the first three places in every event.

5 Sun cream costs money at the first-aid tent.

6 The first-aid tent is next to the changing rooms.

7 You have to pay for water.

8 Only the winner of each event gets a medal.

Exercise C

Writing: Your Opinion

Choose ONE of the two prompts below and write 120–150 words giving your opinion, just like Writing Part 3 in the real MSA exam. This section is graded by your teacher, not automatically.

Choose ONE prompt

Prompt 1: Some people say Sports Day is a great tradition that brings the whole school together. Others think it puts too much pressure on students who are not good at sport. Should schools have a Sports Day? Give your opinion and explain your reasons.

Prompt 2: "Taking part is more important than winning." Do you agree? Write about whether schools should focus on competition and winning, or on fun and taking part, giving reasons for your view.
